title: Separate resolved SSH client policy from mutable input options
description:
The new client API mixes public mutable options, cached resolved policy and per-attempt interaction state in DialOptions (client/dial.go). Resolve returns immediately when its hidden resolved pointer is present (client/config_sources.go, around line 62), even if public fields changed between calls.

Confirmed through public APIs: resolve Host="old.example", change the returned Host to 127.0.0.1, then Dial connects to localhost but verifies/prompts for old.example:<port>. client/trust.go reads the cached trust alias while dialing uses the changed public endpoint. Changes to source or authentication policy may similarly leave derived state stale. Documentation currently forbids mutation during use, leaving between-call reuse ambiguous.

Establish a safe API contract before wider adoption: prefer an immutable resolved connection plan distinct from input options and per-attempt authentication/interaction owners. Keep the endpoint and corresponding trust identity together, preserving explicit HostKeyAlias semantics. If retaining existing signatures, detect and reject modified resolved input or otherwise prevent stale derived state; documentation alone is a weaker guard.

Add regression tests for reuse, changed endpoint/user/port/sources/identity policy and independent connections. Clarify ownership, immutability and concurrency rules without silently changing legacy Connect behavior.
